title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X -> S is a proper smooth curve with connected fibres (genus g). Notation: omega = Omega^1_{X/S}; Omega = f_*omega is the Hodge bundle of rank g; DR = R^1 f_*(Omega^._{X/S}) is relative de Rham cohomology (the '*' in the transcription is the de Rham complex); R^1 f_* O_X ≅ Omega^vee ≅ t, the tangent space of the Jacobian along the zero section.

(1) The Hodge filtration is 0 -> Omega -> DR -> Omega^vee -> 0.

(2) Cup product gives an alternating pairing phi: DR x DR -> R^2 f_*Omega^. ≅ R^1 f_* omega ≅ O_S, i.e. a map Lambda^2 DR -> O_S. Omega is isotropic, and its orthogonal is Omega itself, so Omega is Lagrangian. Hence the induced map DR -> DR^vee is a filtered isomorphism that is the identity on graded pieces. This is the commutative diagram of the two Hodge sequences for DR and DR^vee.

(3) The pairing is already known on Omega x DR and DR x Omega. The only remaining freedom lies in forms on the quotient Omega^vee x Omega^vee, i.e. in Hom(Omega^vee ⊗ Omega^vee, O_S) = Omega ⊗ Omega, and alternation forces it into Lambda^2 Omega. The same point is expressed by the filtration on Lambda^2 DR: Fil^2 = Lambda^2 Omega, gr^1 = Omega ⊗ Omega^vee, gr^0 = Lambda^2 Omega^vee. The pairing kills Fil^2, induces the evaluation pairing on gr^1, and its gr^0-part depends on a choice.

(4) Splittings. Choose a section sigma: Omega^vee -> DR (Grothendieck again writes it 'phi'). Then DR ≅ Omega ⊕ Omega^vee and the form has matrix ((0, id), (-id, phi_0)), where phi_0(t,t') = <sigma t, sigma t'> is an alternating form on Omega^vee, i.e. a section of Lambda^2 Omega.

(5) Change of splitting. Put sigma' = sigma + u with u: Omega^vee -> Omega. Then phi_0'(t,t') = phi_0(t,t') + <t,u(t')> - <t',u(t)>. The change in phi_0 is minus twice the antisymmetric part of u (up to sign convention). Consequences:
- Lagrangian splittings (phi_0 = 0) always exist.
- After 2 is inverted, they form a torsor under the u with zero antisymmetric part, i.e. symmetric u: Omega^vee -> Omega, i.e. Sym^2 Omega (Gamma^2 Omega in general).

Purpose: this is the linear-algebra preliminary for comparing projective connections ('opérateurs hyperboliques', uniformization) on the curve with symplectic splittings of the Hodge filtration of H^1_dR. The next page relates the torsor of such operators to the symplectic splittings, the Gauss–Manin connection and the Kodaira–Spencer map Omega -> Omega^vee ⊗ Omega^1_{S/T}. It also mentions the universal family for abelian varieties with polarization and hyperelliptic curves.
errors: The remark that the indeterminacy in Hom(Omega^vee⊗Omega^vee, O_S) is '=0 (puisqu'il s'agit de formes alternées)' is wrong as stated. Alternating forms on Omega^vee form Lambda^2 Omega, which is nonzero for g ≥ 2. Grothendieck himself immediately treats phi_0 as a possibly nonzero alternating form depending on the splitting. The correct statement: the indeterminacy is only up to the choice of splitting, and it can be killed by choosing a Lagrangian splitting.

Consistency issue with the next page. Lagrangian splittings form a torsor under symmetric tensors Sym^2 Omega (u symmetric), not Lambda^2 Omega. The extension 0 -> Lambda^2 Omega -> Sigma -> O_S on the next page is fine for the space of all (splitting, phi_0) data. But the 'torseur sous Lambda^2' and the factorisation V_{S/T} -> Lambda^2 Omega^vee of Kodaira–Spencer should read Sym^2 (KS is symmetric). This is either a slip or a sign/convention confusion.

Minor: the symbol phi is used both for the pairing and for the section Omega^vee -> DR, which makes the formula phi_0'(t,t') = phi(phi(t)+u(t), phi(t')+u(t')) notationally ambiguous; the stated outcome is otherwise correct.

ideas.what: Hodge filtration of relative H^1_dR of a curve, 0 -> f_*omega -> H^1_dR -> R^1f_*O -> 0, with Omega Lagrangian for the cup-product symplectic form
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration / Lagrangian Hodge subbundle of a polarized VHS of weight 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hodge, Deligne, Griffiths (1960s); algebraic de Rham version Grothendieck/Katz–Oda
ideas.where_published: Algebraic de Rham cohomology appears in Grothendieck's 1966 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' and his Crystals notes; the specific Lagrangian statement is not known to me in his texts

ideas.what: Splittings of the Hodge filtration, matrix form of the symplectic pairing, and Lagrangian splittings forming a torsor under Sym^2 Omega
ideas.modern_name: space of symplectic (Lagrangian) splittings of the Hodge filtration; affine bundle under Sym^2 of the Hodge bundle (cf. almost-holomorphic/quasi-modular forms, Katz's splittings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Katz (p-adic interpolation, 1970s) for unit-root/holomorphic splittings

ideas.what: Set-up to compare projective connections on curves with splittings of H^1_dR, via Gauss–Manin and Kodaira–Spencer (continued on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: projective structures vs symplectic splittings of the Hodge filtration (affine map from the torsor of projective connections to Lagrangian splittings, compatible with Sym^2 H^0(omega) -> H^0(omega^2))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning; Tyurin (1978); Faltings 'Real projective structures on Riemann surfaces' (1983); later Biswas, Bertola–Korotkin–Norton

missed.claim: An algebraic, base-general (over any S) set-up relating the torsor of projective connections ('opérateurs hyperboliques') on a family of curves to Lagrangian splittings of H^1_dR, intended to pass through the universal polarized abelian scheme. Only the linear algebra is done on this page. The comparison is known in the literature, so the novelty is at most the early algebraic and relative formulation.
missed.quote: Pour un splitting de DR par φ: Ω̌ → DR, on a une écriture matricielle ... φ'_0(t,t') = φ_0(t,t') + (t,u(t')) − (t',u(t))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It anticipates algebraic treatments of projective structures and holomorphic anomaly/quasi-modular formalisms, but these are now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard linear algebra of the Hodge filtration of a curve and its symplectic splittings. It is interesting only as the preparatory step toward linking projective connections and uniformization with Hodge splittings, a link documented in the later literature (Tyurin, Faltings, Biswas).
transcription_corrections: 'R^1f_*(Ω^*_{X/S})' should read R^1f_*(Ω^•_{X/S}), the relative de Rham complex.
'l'orth. gourd[?] de Ω^⊥ est Ω' is likely 'l'orthogonal de Ω est Ω' (Omega is Lagrangian).
The matrix is most plausibly ((0, id), (−id, φ_0)); the 'φ id' entry is a corrected/overwritten 'id'.
The second-row middle term of the comparison diagram is the dual DR^vee (written as DR with a check), with the vertical arrow being the map induced by the pairing.
'(t, u(t'))' denotes the duality pairing between Ω^vee and Ω.
